mainTopic: תמד and wine status: מעשר, ברכה, batches of pomace for תרומה, מעשר and הקדש, הכשר, and wine fit for קידוש
overview: The גמרא defends רבא against a משנה about תמד and מעשר. It explains that the משנה chose the equal-volume case only to show how far רבי יהודה goes. רב חייא בר אבין rules that a pomace drink with a wine taste is not wine, only a sour drink. A ברייתא then counts how many soakings of pomace keep the status of the original wine: one batch for מעשר, two for תרומה, three for הקדש. In each case רבי מאיר says the drink stays forbidden as long as it still tastes of wine. A second ברייתא seems to contradict this, and the גמרא answers by splitting the cases: קדושת הגוף versus קדושת דמים, and certain מעשר versus דמאי. רבי יוחנן applies the same batch counting to הכשר, and the גמרא narrows his case step by step, ending with רב פפא's cow that drank the batches. Finally רב rules that קידוש is said only over wine fit for the מזבח. The גמרא asks what this excludes, tries fresh wine from the press, and challenges that suggestion from רבי חייא; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A משנה seems to limit the dispute to the equal-volume case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about תמד and מעשר and infers that the חכמים and רבי יהודה argue only when the drink equals the water. This contradicts רבא's view that they argue even when there is more.
steps.simpleTranslation: A משנה teaches: someone who makes תמד, puts in a measured amount of water, and gets back exactly that amount is exempt from מעשר, but רבי יהודה obligates him. The inference is that they argue only when he gets back the same amount. When he gets back more, everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and reads it closely in order to challenge the view stated earlier in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only describes the case where the liquid came out equal to the water. Since the dispute is placed in that case, the גמרא infers that when more came out, everyone agrees he must separate מעשר because it counts as wine. That clashes with רבא, who said the dispute applies even when more came out.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes תמד, a drink made by soaking grape pomace in water
the same amount as the water he put in
exempt (here, from separating מעשר)
obligates, holds he is required
they only argue in this case (a formula for drawing an inference)

phrases.english: One who makes tamad, and put in water by measure,
and found the same as its measure: he is exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from separating מעשר, even though the grapes were never tithed.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda obligates him.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בִּכְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: They only disagree where it is the same as its measure,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי מִדָּתוֹ – לָא פְּלִיגִי!
phrases.english: but where it is more than its measure, they do not disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בִּכְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's earlier statement in the sugya (before this section).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that the dispute applies even when more liquid came out than water was put in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the משנה places the dispute only in the equal-volume case, it implies that everyone agrees in the larger-volume case.

steps.title: They argue in both cases; the משנה shows the strength of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute applies even when more came out. The משנה chose the equal case to show how far רבי יהודה goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true when more than the measure came out: they argue there too. The משנה mentions the equal case only to show you how strong רבי יהודה's position is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by explaining why the משנה chose the case it did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from the משנה is rejected. The equal-volume case is the hardest case for רבי יהודה, since it looks like nothing more than water. If he obligates even there, he certainly obligates when more came out. The dispute itself covers both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: the same law applies
to show you the strength (the far reach) of someone's opinion

steps.whatToRemember: A משנה often chooses the most extreme case to show how far one opinion goes, so you cannot always infer that a less extreme case is undisputed.

phrases.english: The same is true, that even
where it is more than its measure, they disagree;
and the fact that they disagree about the same as its measure
is to tell you the strength of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי מִדָּתוֹ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case choice: the משנה uses the extreme case to show how far רבי יהודה goes (כחו דרבי יהודה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's choice of case implies agreement when more liquid came out.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue in both cases; the equal case was chosen to show that רבי יהודה obligates even there.

steps.title: Does תמד that tastes like wine count as wine?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רב חייא בר אבין about the status of תמד from שמרים that has the taste of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק asked רב חייא בר אבין: what is the law about שמרים that have the taste of wine?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: whether a drink made from soaked שמרים that tastes like wine counts as wine, for example for its ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a wine flavor is enough to give the drink the status of wine, which would mean the ברכה of בורא פרי הגפן. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him
pomace or lees, the leftovers of pressed grapes
what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak asked
of Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמָרִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן טַעַם יַיִן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Pomace that has the taste of wine, what is it?
phrases.notes: He means the drink made by soaking this pomace in water. Which ברכה does it get?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of מעשר on תמד to whether wine-flavored תמד counts as wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pomace drink with a wine taste has the status of wine.

steps.title: It is not wine, just a sour drink
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין answers that such a drink is not wine. It is merely a sharp, sour-tasting beverage.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think it is wine? It is just a sour drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין answers that a wine taste does not make this drink wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine flavor is only a sharpness that soaked into the water, so the drink does not get the status of real wine. It therefore does not get the ברכה of wine.

keyTerms.meaning: do you think?
wine
a sour or sharp-tasting drink
merely, just

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ חַמְרָא הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think it is wine?
It is merely a sour drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ חַמְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pomace drink with a wine taste is not wine. It is only a sour drink.

steps.title: Pomace of תרומה: first and second batches forbidden, third permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when תמד is made again and again from שמרים of תרומה, the first two batches are forbidden to a זר and the third is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: with שמרים of תרומה, the first and second batches are forbidden, and the third is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about reusing שמרים of תרומה to make several batches of תמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time the שמרים are soaked again, the drink gets weaker. The first two batches still carry enough of the wine to keep the status of תרומה, so a non-כהן may not drink them. By the third batch the drink is weak enough to be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion given to a כהן, forbidden to a non-כהן
the first and second batches
the third batch

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Pomace of teruma:
the first and second are forbidden,
phrases.notes: These are the first and second batches of drink made by soaking the same pomace again and again.

phrases.english: and the third is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁמָרִים שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of pomace drinks, now regarding תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From pomace of תרומה, the first and second batches are forbidden to a non-כהן, and the third is permitted.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: even the third batch is forbidden if it tastes of wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and holds that even the third batch is forbidden if it still gives off the taste of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: even the third batch is forbidden, if it gives off a taste of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר, the dissenting opinion in the ברייתא, makes the third batch depend on taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets a fixed count: by the third batch, the drink is permitted. רבי מאיר says it depends on taste. If the third batch still has the flavor of the תרומה wine, it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: even, also
when it gives off flavor

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא disagrees about pomace of תרומה: the חכמים permit the third batch outright, while רבי מאיר forbids it if it still tastes of wine.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Even the third, when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף שְׁלִישִׁי, בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the dissenting view to the first opinion in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the third batch from pomace of תרומה is forbidden if it still imparts the taste of wine.

steps.title: Watered pomace of second tithe: first batch forbidden, second permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: for שמרים of מעשר שני, the first batch of תמד is forbidden and the second is permitted. רבי מאיר says even the second is forbidden if it still tastes of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with pomace of מעשר שני, the first batch is forbidden and the second is permitted. רבי מאיר says: even the second is forbidden if it gives off the taste of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 5 keeps going. It now applies the same counting idea to the leftover pomace of מעשר שני wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, two batches were forbidden. Here only the first batch keeps the status of מעשר שני. רבי מאיר keeps his same position from Step 6: what matters is whether the taste of wine is still there, not the number of batches.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני: produce that may only be eaten or drunk in ירושלים
The first batch of water poured onto the pomace
The second batch
Gives off taste; the drink still tastes of wine

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר – רִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר, שֵׁנִי מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And of tithe – the first is forbidden, the second is permitted.
phrases.notes: "Forbidden" here means it has to be drunk in ירושלים like מעשר שני.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף שֵׁנִי, בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: even the second, when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from תרומה to מעשר שני
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First batch from מעשר שני pomace is forbidden and the second is permitted. רבי מאיר forbids the second too if it tastes of wine.

steps.title: Watered pomace of consecrated wine: up to the third forbidden, fourth permitted
steps.stepSummary: For שמרים of הקדש, the batches up to and including the third are forbidden, and the fourth is permitted. רבי מאיר forbids even the fourth if it tastes of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with pomace of הקדש, the third batch is forbidden and the fourth is permitted. רבי מאיר says: even the fourth is forbidden if it gives off the taste of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list with wine that was given to the בית המקדש. Here the holiness lasts longer than with תרומה or מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a ladder here: מעשר holds for one batch, תרומה for two, and הקדש for three. רבי מאיר again says the test is taste, not counting.

keyTerms.meaning: Property given to the בית המקדש; one may not benefit from it
The third batch
The fourth batch

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא sets up a ladder: מעשר holds for 1 batch, תרומה for 2, and הקדש for 3. רבי מאיר always says it stays forbidden as long as it tastes of wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ – שְׁלִישִׁי אָסוּר, וּרְבִיעִי מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And of consecrated property – the third is forbidden, and the fourth is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף רְבִיעִי, בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: even the fourth, when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the last category, הקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From הקדש pomace, the batches up to the third are forbidden and the fourth is permitted. רבי מאיר forbids the fourth too if it tastes of wine.

steps.title: A different teaching contradicts both rulings
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says תמד of הקדש is always forbidden and תמד of מעשר is always permitted. This clashes with the first ברייתא on both points.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא points out a contradiction: of הקדש, it is always forbidden, and of מעשר, it is always permitted. So הקדש contradicts הקדש, and מעשר contradicts מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that gives the opposite results, and says the two sources seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said הקדש becomes permitted at the fourth batch, but the second says it never becomes permitted. The first said the first batch of מעשר is forbidden, but the second says even that one is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: "And raise a contradiction": one source is set against another
Always, no matter how many batches
It is difficult; there is a contradiction

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
of consecrated property – it is always forbidden,
and of tithe – it is always permitted.
Consecrated property is difficult against consecrated property,
tithe is difficult against tithe!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rulings of Steps 7 and 8 from a different ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings about הקדש and מעשר in the first ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives opposite results for both categories: הקדש is never permitted, and מעשר is permitted even at the first batch.

steps.title: Consecrated pomace: inherent holiness versus value holiness
steps.stepSummary: The הקדש contradiction is solved: one ברייתא speaks of קדושת הגוף, the other of קדושת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הקדש contradiction is not difficult: here it is קדושת הגוף, and there it is קדושת דמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the הקדש part of the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about two different kinds of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "always forbidden" ruling is about wine that is holy in itself (קדושת הגוף), which is the stronger kind. The ruling that permits the fourth batch is about wine that was dedicated only for its money value (קדושת דמים), which is weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of the item itself, set aside for use in the בית המקדש
Holiness of value: dedicated only for the money it is worth
Here / there: one source is talking about this case

phrases.english: Consecrated property against consecrated property is not difficult –
here, with inherent sanctity,
phrases.notes: This "here" is the ברייתא that says it is always forbidden.

phrases.english: there, with sanctity of value.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶקְדֵּשׁ אַהֶקְדֵּשׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הקדש half of the קשיא in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks of a different kind of הקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות were talking about the same kind of הקדש
steps.terutzMaskana: קדושת הגוף is always forbidden; קדושת דמים becomes permitted at the fourth batch

steps.title: Tithe pomace: certain tithe versus doubtful produce
steps.stepSummary: The מעשר contradiction is solved: one ברייתא speaks of certain מעשר, the other of מעשר from דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מעשר contradiction is also not difficult: here it is certain מעשר, and there it is מעשר of דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the contradiction in the same way, by splitting the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that forbids the first batch is about real, certain מעשר שני. The ruling that always permits it is about מעשר taken from דמאי, produce that might already have been tithed. Since that is only a doubt, the rule is more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain; here, wine whose status as מעשר שני is definite (not from דמאי)
Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may or may not have been tithed
Also

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are solved by splitting the cases. Strong holiness (קדושת הגוף, certain מעשר) is treated strictly, and weak holiness (קדושת דמים, דמאי) is treated leniently.

phrases.english: Tithe against tithe is also not difficult –
here, with certain tithe,
phrases.notes: This "here" is the first ברייתא, where the first batch is forbidden.

phrases.english: there, with tithe of doubtful produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֵׂר אַמַּעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מעשר half of the קשיא, finishing the answer begun in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: certain מעשר versus דמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות were talking about the same kind of מעשר
steps.terutzMaskana: Certain מעשר makes the first batch forbidden; מעשר from דמאי is always permitted

steps.title: The same counting applies to making food susceptible to impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, teaches that the batch counting used for these prohibitions also applies to הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: just as they ruled about their prohibition, so they ruled about their הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is added. The same batch-counting rules about when תמד still counts as wine also decide its status for הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was only whether the drink is forbidden. רבי יוחנן extends the same lines to a second area of law, whether the liquid makes food able to become impure. A batch that counts as wine for prohibition counts as wine for הכשר too, and a batch that does not count, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Their prohibition
Their ability to make food susceptible to טומאה (הכשר)
Just as, in the same way that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the line where תמד stops counting as wine is one consistent line, used for both איסור and טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
In the same way that they said regarding their prohibition,
so they said regarding their rendering susceptible.
phrases.notes: Some liquids make food able to become impure. This applies the same batch count to that question.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the batch-counting rules from prohibition to הכשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The batch counts that decide whether תמד is forbidden also decide whether it causes הכשר.

steps.title: Why does it matter for הכשר whether תמד is wine or water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 12. Both wine and water make food able to become טמא, so the batch counting should make no difference for הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making food susceptible: what difference does the kind of liquid make? If it counts as water, it makes food susceptible. If it counts as wine, it also makes food susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's rule from step 12. Water and wine both make food ready to become טמא, so why count batches at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting batches tells us whether the תמד counts as wine or as water. For הכשר, both wine and water are on the list of liquids that make food susceptible. So the answer seems to change nothing, and רבי יוחנן's rule looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food able to become טמא, which happens once it gets wet with certain liquids
They do make food susceptible
A weak drink made by soaking grape leftovers in water

phrases.english: Their making food susceptible — what kind of liquid is it?
phrases.notes: This refers back to step 12, where רבי יוחנן said the batch counting also applies to הכשר.

phrases.english: If it counts as water, it makes food susceptible!
If it counts as wine, it makes food susceptible!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶכְשֵׁירָן דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical relevance of רבי יוחנן's rule in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the batch counting applies to הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine and water both make food susceptible, so whether תמד counts as wine or as water changes nothing for הכשר.

steps.title: The case is תמד made with rainwater
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed when the תמד was made with rainwater. That water does not make food susceptible unless a person wanted it, so here it matters whether the liquid counts as wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he made the תמד with rainwater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case to תמד made from rainwater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rainwater that fell without a person wanting it does not make food susceptible. If such תמד counts as wine, it does make food susceptible. If it counts as water, it does not. Now the batch counting makes a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for this specific case
Rainwater

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he made the תמד with rainwater.
phrases.notes: The point is rainwater he never planned to use. That kind of water only makes food susceptible if a person wanted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁתִּמְּדוֹ בְּמֵי גְשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every kind of תמד makes food susceptible, whether it counts as wine or as water
steps.terutzMaskana: With rainwater nobody wanted, only תמד that counts as wine makes food susceptible, so the batch counting matters

steps.title: Putting the rainwater into the vessel shows he wanted it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if he took the rainwater and poured it onto the grape leftovers, he clearly wanted that water. Then it makes food susceptible even if it counts as water.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he took the water and poured it into the vessel, he has shown that he wants it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rainwater makes food susceptible once a person shows he wants it. Taking the water and pouring it into the container shows exactly that. So even the later batches, which count as water, should make food susceptible, and the batch counting no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes and pours
A vessel or container
He has shown he values them, meaning he wants to use them

phrases.english: But since he takes and pours
them into the vessel, he has shown he wants them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל וְרָמֵי לְהוּ לְמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case set up in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of תמד made with rainwater
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring the water into the vessel shows he wants it, and water a person wants makes food susceptible.

steps.title: The תמד formed on its own
steps.stepSummary: The case is where nobody poured the water. Rain fell on the grape leftovers, and the תמד formed by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where it turned into תמד by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case further: no person poured the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rain fell onto the leftovers by itself, nobody showed he wanted the water. So the water still lacks the person's wanting, and only the wine status can make food susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: It became תמד by itself

phrases.english: No, it is needed where it turned into תמד by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁנִּתַּמֵּד מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person poured the rainwater himself and so showed he wanted it
steps.terutzMaskana: The rain fell by itself, so no person showed he wanted the water

steps.title: Drawing off each batch shows he wants the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again. When he draws off each batch so more can form, he shows he wants the water, so it should make food susceptible anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he draws off each batch one after another, he has shown he wants them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the תמד first formed by itself, the person keeps drawing off batch after batch. That act shows he wants the liquid. If so, the later batches make food susceptible even when they count as water.

keyTerms.meaning: Draws off, pulls out the liquid
Each one in turn, one batch after another

phrases.english: But since he draws it off,
each batch one after another, he has shown he wants them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּקָא נָגֵיד קַמָּא קַמָּא אַחְשְׁבִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case set up in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of תמד that formed by itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drawing off each batch shows he wants the liquid, which gives the water the power to make food susceptible.

steps.title: רב פפא: a cow drank the batches
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that no person drew off the batches. A cow drank each batch in turn, so no person ever showed he wanted the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case of a cow that drinks each batch one after another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the last challenge by changing who removed the batches: an animal, not a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow drinking the liquid is not a person showing he wants it. So the batches still lack anyone's wanting. Whether they make food susceptible depends only on whether they count as wine, and the batch counting of step 12 makes a real difference. This ends the defense of רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A cow
Each first one in turn, batch after batch

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule that batch counting applies to הכשר matters only for rainwater nobody wanted. The case is תמד that formed by itself and was drunk by a cow, so no person ever showed he wanted the water.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
It is a case of a cow that drinks each batch one after another.
phrases.notes: A person did not draw off the batches here, so nobody showed he wanted the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּפָרָה שֶׁשּׁוֹתָה רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and closes the discussion of הכשר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person drew off each batch and so showed he wanted the water
steps.terutzMaskana: A cow drank the batches, so no person ever showed he wanted the water

steps.title: רב: קידוש only on wine fit for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רב זוטרא בר טוביה quotes רב: קידוש is said only over wine good enough to be poured on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: We say קידוש only over wine that is fit to be poured on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about which wine may be used for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ties the wine for קידוש to the standard of wine used for נסכים in the בית המקדש. Wine that would not be accepted on the מזבח cannot be used for קידוש. This sets up a discussion of which kinds of wine pass that test.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctifying the day, said over wine on שבת
To be poured as a wine offering
The altar in the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for which wine may be used for קידוש, and the following discussion will test which wines meet the מזבח standard.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said that רב said:
We do not say the sanctification of the day,
except over wine
that is fit to be poured on top of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about wine, following the earlier discussion of wine and תמד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידוש may be said only over wine fit to be poured as a נסך on the מזבח

steps.title: What does רב's rule leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which wine רב meant to rule out when he said קידוש needs wine fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule is meant to exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: which kind of wine is רב trying to rule out? The next step tries one answer and challenges it, and the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that says 'only wine fit for the מזבח' must be leaving some wine out. The גמרא wants to know exactly which wine fails the test. This question opens the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to rule out
What?

phrases.english: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: He is asking about רב's rule from the last step: wine fit for the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רב's rule from step 19 is meant to exclude.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of wine is unfit for קידוש under רב's rule

steps.title: Fresh wine from the press cannot be what is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב excludes fresh wine from the press. It then challenges this from רבי חייא, who says such wine is valid for the מזבח if it was already brought. So it should be fine for קידוש even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the rule excludes wine fresh from the press, that is a problem. רבי חייא taught: one should not bring wine fresh from his press for the מזבח, but if he did bring it, it is valid. Since it is valid if he brought it, for us (for קידוש) it should be fine even from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer: maybe רב means fresh wine from the press. Then it attacks that answer using a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא says fresh wine should not be brought to the מזבח from the start, but it is כשר if it was brought. That means it is still 'fit for the מזבח' in some way. Since רב's test for קידוש is only that the wine be fit for the מזבח, fresh wine passes the test, so it cannot be what רב excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; a suggested answer the גמרא is about to test
Wine fresh from the press, not yet aged
But didn't (someone) teach? Opens a challenge from a ברייתא
From the start; the preferred way of doing it
If he already brought it, it counts (בדיעבד)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two areas. רבי חייא's 'not from the start' is about the מזבח. The גמרא's point is that for קידוש, all we need is wine that is fit for the מזבח at all, so the 'from the start' limit does not carry over.

phrases.english: If you say it is to exclude wine fresh from his press,
but didn't רבי חייא teach:
One should not bring wine fresh from his press,
but if he brought it, it is valid;
and since if he brought it, it is valid,
we may use it even from the start too!
phrases.notes: 'We' means us making קידוש, as opposed to the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי יַיִן מִגִּתּוֹ, וְהָא תָּאנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 20's question and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes fresh wine from the press
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא rules fresh wine valid for the מזבח after the fact, so it counts as fit for the מזבח. Since קידוש only needs wine fit for the מזבח, fresh wine should be allowed for קידוש even from the start.
